"'''Mazey Day'''" is the fourth episode of the sixth series of the anthology series ''[[Black Mirror]]''. It was written by series creator [[Charlie Brooker]] and directed by [[Uta Briesewitz]]. Alongside the rest of the sixth series, it premiered on Netflix on 15 June 2023. It tells the story of Bo ([[Zazie Beetz]]), a [[paparazzo]], and Mazey Day ([[Clara Rugaard]]), an actress hiding from the media after a car accident.

It is the first [[supernatural horror]] episode in the show. Brooker wrote it after the sixth series episode "[[Demon 79]]", another horror story, and aimed to broaden the scope of the programme. Filming took place in June 2022 in Spain.

Set in 2006, the depicted paparazzi pursuit of Mazey was compared to media attention on Britney Spears, Paris Hilton, and Lindsay Lohan. The episode's [[plot twist|twist]] was widely criticised by reviewers, along with the episode's premise and themes. Many critics considered "Mazey Day" the worst episode of the sixth series and one of the worst in the show.

== Plot ==
In 2006, a [[paparazza]] named Bo ([[Zazie Beetz]]) takes photographic evidence at a motel of a male celebrity having an affair with a man. He offers her $500 to delete the photos, but she sells them for $300 each, and the celebrity kills himself. Bo's colleagues Hector ([[Danny Ramirez]]), Whitty (Robbie Tann), and Duke (James P. Rees) are unsympathetic. They harass a celebrity whose [[sex tape]] has gone public: Whitty provokes her with misogynistic slurs and threatens legal action when she reacts. Bo decides to quit the profession.

The actress Mazey Day ([[Clara Rugaard]]) quits a film shoot in the Czech Republic after a [[hit and run]] under the influence of wine and [[hallucinogenic mushrooms]] and disappears from the public eye. A $30,000 reward is offered for the first image of her. Bo, who has been confronted by her flatmate Nathan ([[David Rysdahl]]) over late rent, tracks Mazey to a film producer's mansion via a takeaway place Mazey had mentioned in a magazine article. Mazey trashes the living room that night and Dr. Babich (Kenneth Collard) arranges for her to stay at a [[New Age]] rehab for the weekend. Bo follows the car but the driver stops at a diner to slash her tyres. She calls Hector to take them on a motorbike to the rehab compound; Hector is unaware that Whitty has placed a tracker on the motorbike and so Whitty arrives shortly afterwards with Duke.

The four paparazzi break into the compound and find Mazey chained up in a cabin with goats. As Bo undoes her chains, the others take dozens of photos. Mazey warns them to leave. As the [[full moon]] emerges, Mazey turns into a [[werewolf]]. Whitty and Duke continue taking pictures and are killed, and Bo and Hector try to escape. Hector's motorbike is struck by a car and the driver is attacked by the werewolf as Bo and Hector run through the woods. They make it to the diner and beg a police officer, Clay ([[Corey Johnson (actor)|Corey Johnson]]), to call for backup. Bo lunges to take his gun and he begins to restrain and handcuff her.

The werewolf arrives and kills or wounds everybody except Bo, who manages to shoot her with the police officer's handgun. Hector hands Bo his camera as he dies. Mazey, now heavily bleeding in human form, begs Bo to shoot her. Bo hands her the gun, and as Mazey points the gun at her own head, Bo prepares to take a photograph. A gunshot is heard.

== Production ==
''Black Mirror'' went on hiatus after its fifth series was released in 2019. Its executive producers, [[Charlie Brooker]] and [[Annabel Jones]], departed from the production company House of Tomorrow and joined Broke and Bones, leading to negotiations for production rights.<ref name="Variety Endemol">{{cite web | url = https://variety.com/2020/tv/news/black-mirror-charlie-brooker-annabel-jones-netflix-endemol-shine-group-1203478778/ | title = 'Black Mirror' break from ''Black Mirror'' and worked on more comedic projects.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/news/on-demand/2020-05-04/black-mirror-6-update/|title=Charlie Brooker gives Black Mirror season 6 update: "I don't know what stomach there would be for stories about societies falling apart"|work=[[Radio Times]]|last=Morris|first=Lauren|date=4 May 2020|access-date=10 May 2020|archive-date=10 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200510164108/https://www.radiotimes.com/news/on-demand/2020-05-04/black-mirror-6-update/|url-status=live}}</ref> In May 2022, [[Netflix]] announced that a sixth ''Black Mirror'' series was in development. Broke and Bones produced the series, while House of Tomorrow's parent company, [[Banijay]], retained ownership.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Ravindran |first1=Manori |title=''Black Mirror'' Returns: New Series in the Works at Netflix (Exclusive) |url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/global/black-mirror-season-6-netflix-1235266891/ |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20230615060651/https://variety.com/2022/tv/global/black-mirror-season-6-netflix-1235266891/ |archive-date=15 June 2023 |date=16 May 2022 |url-status=live |access-date=15 June 2023 }}</ref>

Brooker was the screenwriter for "Mazey Day".<ref name="EW titles">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-episode-titles-photos/|title=''Black Mirror'' season 6 reveals episode details, new photos|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|last=Holub|first=Christian|date=11 May 2023|accessdate=24 July 2023|archive-date=15 June 2023|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20230615060641/https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-episode-titles-photos/|url-status=live}}</ref> At 40 minutes, it is the shortest episode of the programme.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.cosmopolitan.com/uk/entertainment/a44170793/netflix-black-mirror-mazey-day-episode-explained/|title=Netflix's Black Mirror: Mazey Day episode explained|magazine=[[Cosmopolitan (magazine)|Cosmopolitan]]|last=Venn|first=Lydia|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=16 June 2023}}</ref> According to Brooker, the early 2000s placed the setting before "everyone was a paparazzo" due to smartphones, where photographic evidence was much harder to forge.<ref name="NME interview"/> Other episodes in the series also had period settings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-season-6-red-mirror-newsupdate/|title=Black Mirror creator Charlie Brooker explains 'Red Mirror' label|work=[[Radio Times]]|last1=Griffin|first1=Louise|last2=Cormack|first2=Morgan|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=17 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616225949/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-season-6-red-mirror-newsupdate/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The first episode of the sixth series to be written was "[[Demon 79]]", a horror story set in 1979. Brooker said this episode, labelled as ''Red Mirror'', helped him find a new perspective for the series, closer to "people are fucked up" than "tech is bad".<ref name="Esquire interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a44197628/charlie-brooker-black-mirror-interview/|title=''Black Mirror'' Season 6: Charlie Brooker Breaks Down Every Episode|work=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]|last=Stefansky|first=Emma|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=17 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616145405/https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a44197628/charlie-brooker-black-mirror-interview/|url-status=live}}</ref> In writing "Mazey Day", Brooker considered "[[The National Anthem (Black Mirror)|The National Anthem]]", the first episode, which "was obviously designed to be startling and surprising and weird". A ''Red Mirror'' title sequence for "Mazey Day" was made, but Brooker eventually chose the ''Black Mirror'' opening titles to conceal the supernatural twist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-six-charlie-brooker-spoilers|title=''Black Mirror''{{'}}s Charlie Brooker Keeps Finding New Ways to Freak Us Out|work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|last=Press|first=Joy|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=2 August 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616162024/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-six-charlie-brooker-spoilers|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="DoG review"/> Brooker said that ideally, the titles would change to ''Red Mirror'' on repeat viewings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/sam_cleal/black-mirror-netflix-facts|date=June 16, 2023|title=Here Are 17 Interesting "Black Mirror" Season Six Facts We Learned In Conversation With Charlie Brooker|last=Cleal|first=Sam|website=[[BuzzFeed News]]|accessdate=June 18, 2023|archive-date=18 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230618202937/https://www.buzzfeed.com/sam_cleal/black-mirror-netflix-facts|url-status=live}}</ref> As of April 2025 the title has since been changed from ''Black Mirror'' to ''Red Mirror'' in the episode's opening sequence on Netflix.

=== Casting and filming ===

|title=''Black Mirror'' Cast Revealed: Aaron Paul, Josh Hartnett, Paapa Essiedu, Kate Mara and Zazie Beetz Join New Season (Exclusive) |access-date=15 June 2023}}</ref> The director was [[Uta Briesewitz]].<ref name="EW titles"/> Udo Kramer designed the sets for "Mazey Day", as well as the other series six episodes.<ref>{{cite |url=https://deadline.com/2022/08/zazie-beetz-confirms-she-just-finished-filming-her-black-mirror-episode-1235082867/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] [[province of Málaga]], under the name "Red Book". Locations included [[Marbella]], [[Estepona]] and the Loasur studios in [[Coín]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.surinenglish.com/malaga/netflix-black-mirror-20220624114708-nt.html|title=The long-awaited Netflix series Black Mirror returns and one episode is being shot entirely in Malaga province|work=[[Diario Sur]]|first=Francisco|last=Griñán|date=24 June 2022|accessdate=2 August 2023|archive-date=23 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723175932/https://www.surinenglish.com/malaga/netflix-black-mirror-20220624114708-nt.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Running through the woods at night felt dangerous, Beetz reported, though some scenes set at night were filmed during the day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/showbiz/celebrity-news/atlanta-netflix-spain-charlie-brooker-aaron-paul-b1088349.html|title=Atlanta star Zazie Beetz says filming for Black Mirror was 'hazardous'|work=[[Evening Standard]]|last=Roberts|first=Hannah|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=4 August 2023|archive-date=5 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705042700/https://www.standard.co.uk/showbiz/celebrity-news/atlanta-netflix-spain-charlie-brooker-aaron-paul-b1088349.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Framestore]] worked on visual effects for the werewolf, including [[skeletal animation|rigging]] for a digital double of Rugaard transforming into the creature. The werewolf's teeth underwent many iterations and a dedicated system for bones breaking and shifting was developed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fxguide.com/quicktakes/framestores-black-mirror-mazey-day-frenzy/|title=Framestore's Black Mirror 'Mazey Day' Frenzy|last=Seymour|first=Mike|work=[[fxguide]]|date=21 July 2023|accessdate=8 August 2023}}</ref> The company NVIZ provided [[compositing]] of graphics such as computer and television screens and worked on redesigning Málaga backgrounds to resemble Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nviz-studio.com/black_mirror_6.html|title=Black Mirror Season 6|publisher=NVIZ Studio|accessdate=2 August 2023|archive-date=23 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723173243/https://nviz-studio.com/black_mirror_6.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The soundtrack was composed by Ariel Marx and released on 21 July 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://filmmusicreporter.com/2023/07/21/soundtrack-album-for-black-mirror-episode-mazey-day-released/|title=Soundtrack Album for 'Black Mirror' Episode 'Mazey Day' Released|work=Film Music Reporter|date=21 July 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=22 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230722092506/http://filmmusicreporter.com/2023/07/21/soundtrack-album-for-black-mirror-episode-mazey-day-released/|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Ron Galella, 1988.jpg|thumb|upright|alt=Ron Galella|The paparazzo [[Ron Galella]], subject of ''[[Smash His Camera]]'']]
According to Beetz, the actors improvised slang and cultural references to the era. The attitude of paparazzi to young female celebrities in 2006 was considered.<ref name="Collider"/> Rugaard watched documentaries on [[Britney Spears]] and [[Amy Winehouse]], while Beetz and Ramirez watched ''[[Smash His Camera]]'' (2010), to compare Bo's motivations to the paparazzo [[Ron Galella]].<ref name="Collider">{{cite web|url=https://collider.com/black-mirror-season-6-mazey-day-zazie-beetz-danny-ramirez-clara-rugaard-interview/|title='Black Mirror' Season 6: The "Mazey Day" Cast Knew They Were Making a Period Piece|work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|last=Lane|first=Carly|date=23 June 2023|accessdate=2 August 2023|archive-date=5 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705052716/https://collider.com/black-mirror-season-6-mazey-day-zazie-beetz-danny-ramirez-clara-rugaard-interview/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/global/black-mirror-anjana-vasan-1235645165/|title='Black Mirror' Star Anjana Vasan Talks 'Demon 79,' Working With Charlie Brooker and Color Blind Casting|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|last=Ramachandran|first=Naman|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=24 July 2023|archive-date=24 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724132927/https://variety.com/2023/tv/global/black-mirror-anjana-vasan-1235645165/|url-status=live}}</ref> Beetz said Bo had self-loathing and chose not to empathise with people more privileged than herself.<ref name="THR"/> Ramirez commented that each character's [[shadow self]] is seen, as they are driven by both good and bad qualities.<ref name="THR"/>

Beetz believed that there was a difference between interviewing a celebrity and taking pictures without their consent. Ramirez commented that "the system itself" is at fault: while Hector or Bo invade people's privacy, they are forced to make money to pay rent.<ref name="THR"/> Beetz said the episode had a "tongue-in-cheek dark element".<ref name="Deadline"/> She said the message is that a person who reveals others' secrets will end up "raw and exposed" themselves.<ref name="TheWrap">{{cite web|url=https://www.thewrap.com/black-mirror-episode-4-ending-explained-zazie-beetz/|title='Black Mirror' Star Zazie Beetz Unpacks Episode 4's Shocking, Transformative Twist: 'Leaves Everybody Raw and Exposed'|work=[[TheWrap]]|last=Seitz|first=Loree|date=19 June 2023|accessdate=2 August 2023|archive-date=23 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723141928/https://www.thewrap.com/black-mirror-episode-4-ending-explained-zazie-beetz/|url-status=live}}</ref> The episode uses the supernatural in place of technology, but Beetz said it led to "the same exploration of the human condition".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-goes-supernatural-mazey-day/|title=How Black Mirror season 6 defies genre expectations|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|last=Holub|first=Christian|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=2 August 2023|archive-date=28 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230728082813/https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-goes-supernatural-mazey-day/|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Clara Rugaard en la presentación de "El amor en su lugar" ("Love Gets a Room"), Madrid, 2021 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|alt=Clara Rugaard|[[Clara Rugaard]] in 2021]]
Rugaard said that Mazey "just wants to exist in the world undisturbed". However, she had unwittingly entered a [[Faustian bargain]] where her acting success brought her into the public eye. Though she is commoditised and has fans who worship her, Mazey is lonely.<ref name="THR"/> Rugaard said that, as a werewolf, Mazey gets to regain control.<ref name="TheWrap"/>

== Analysis ==
"Mazey Day", a [[supernatural horror|horror]] story, is the first ''Black Mirror'' episode to feature the supernatural. It has elements of [[fantasy]], another uncommon genre for the programme.<ref name="Vulture"/><ref name="Mashable">{{cite web|url=https://mashable.com/article/black-mirror-season-6-mazey-day-explained|title='Black Mirror' Season 6: The "Mazey Day" episode explained|work=[[Mashable]]|last=Hamadeh|first=Yasmeen|date=17 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=29 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230729055410/https://mashable.com/article/black-mirror-season-6-mazey-day-explained|url-status=live}}</ref> It is less focused on technology than other instalments.<ref name="AVClub"/> Like the previous episodes "The National Anthem" and "[[Smithereens (Black Mirror)|Smithereens]]", all featured technology exists today,<ref name="RT"/> centrally the camera.<ref name="RS"/> To establish the setting, the 2006 birth of [[Suri Cruise]] is announced at the start of the episode.<ref name="DoG review"/> An [[iPod]] and mention of the [[Iraq War]] also indicate the era.<ref name="Vulture"/> Reference is made to ''Sea of Tranquility'', a fictional programme from other episodes.<ref name="Vulture"/>

2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705184506/https://screenrant.com/black-mirror-mazey-day-backlash-misses-point/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]''{{'}}s Abbey White commented that the episode explores what it means to be a "monster".<ref name="THR">{{cite magazine |last1=White |first1=Abbey |title=''Black Mirror'' Stars Zazie Beetz, Danny Ramirez on the Tragedy and Monstrosities Behind "Mazey Day" |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/black-mirror-zazie-beetz-danny-ramirez-mazey-day-season-6-1235519942/ |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=21 June 2023 |accessdate=2 August 2023}}</ref> Writing in ''[[The Verge]]'', Andrew Webster compared Bo's enticement into chasing Mazey to a [[heist film]] trope of convincing criminals into "one last job".<ref name="Verge">{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/23763326/black-mirror-mazey-day-review-season-6-netflix|title=Black Mirror's 'Mazey Day' is a brisk, bloody bite of celebrity crisis|work=[[The Verge]]|last=Webster|first=Andrew|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=24 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724170744/https://www.theverge.com/23763326/black-mirror-mazey-day-review-season-6-netflix|url-status=live}}</ref>

In Mazey's car accident, she injures a werewolf that bites her as she exits the vehicle.<ref name="RT">{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-mazey-day-ending-explained/|title=Black Mirror: Mazey Day ending explained - What just happened?|work=[[Radio Times]]|last=Hibbs|first=James|date=20 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=23 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230623033347/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-mazey-day-ending-explained/|url-status=live}}</ref> During the crash, a full moon is visible in the sky; police later say a human corpse was found at the scene.<ref name="Mashable"/> The audience initially believes Mazey's distress comes from guilt and addiction.<ref name="DoG review"/><ref name="Mashable"/> The twist is foreshadowed by dialogue from Mazey's doctor and goats left in the rehab for the werewolf to consume.<ref name="Mashable"/> Mazey plays "[[Supermassive Black Hole (song)|Supermassive Black Hole]]" by [[Muse (band)|Muse]], which is prominently used in ''[[The Twilight Saga (film series)|The Twilight Saga]]'', a film series about werewolves and vampires.<ref name="Mashable"/> Though the production were aware of the connection before the episode's release, the song was not a deliberate reference.<ref name="NME interview">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.nme.com/features/tv-features/black-mirror-netflix-interview-charlie-brooker-cast-episodes-theories-3457066|title='Black Mirror' season six post-watch guide: trivia, set secrets and more|magazine=[[NME]]|last=Flood|first=Alex|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=16 June 2023}}</ref>

Describing [[consent]] as a focal point, White wrote that Bo and Hector are less aggressive than the white men—Nathan and Duke—in invading subjects' privacy.<ref name="THR"/> Harrisson thought the police's dismissiveness of Bo could relate to race, a recurring idea in the sixth series.<ref name="DoG order"/> However, Ben Rosenstock of ''[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]'' saw the officer's reaction as reasonable in context.<ref name="Vulture">{{cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-recap-season-6-episode-4-mazey-day-explained.html|title=''Black Mirror'' Recap: Shoot for the Moon|work=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]|last=Rosenstock|first=Ben|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=29 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230629000342/https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-recap-season-6-episode-4-mazey-day-explained.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Reception ==
On the review aggregator [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the episode holds an approval rating of 57% based on 14 reviews.<ref>{{cite Rotten Tomatoes |type=tv |id=black_mirror |season=6 |episode=4 |access-date=3 August 2023}}</ref> Out of five stars, the episode received two stars in ''Vulture'', ''[[i (newspaper)|i]]'' and ''The Independent'',<ref name="Vulture"/><ref name="i"/><ref name="Indy"/> three stars in ''Den of Geek'',<ref name="DoG review"/> and five stars in ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]''.<ref name="Tele"/> Rosenstock, ''[[BBC Culture]]''{{'}}s Neil Armstrong and ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]''{{'}}s Judy Berman saw it as the worst episode of the series,<ref name="Vulture"/><ref name="Time">{{cite magazine|url=https://time.com/6287513/black-mirror-season-6-review/|title=What Even Is ''Black Mirror'' Anymore?|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|last=Berman|first=Judy|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=15 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715005440/https://time.com/6287513/black-mirror-season-6-review/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BBC">{{cite web |last=Armstrong |first=Neil |title=Black Mirror season six review: Charlie Brooker's series is 'a show that revels in its twists' |url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20230614-black-mirror-season-six-review-charlie-brookers-series-is-a-show-that-revels-in-its-twists |website=[[BBC Culture]] |date=15 June 2023 |accessdate=3 August 2023 |archive-date=20 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720174319/https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20230614-black-mirror-season-six-review-charlie-brookers-series-is-a-show-that-revels-in-its-twists |url-status=live }}</ref> and Leila Jordan of ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' thought it was one of the worst in the show.<ref name="Paste">{{cite web|url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/tv/netflix/black-mirror-season-6-review|title=''Black Mirror'' Struggles to Imagine the Future in an Uneven Season 6|work=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]|last=Jordan|first=Leila|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=24 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724170744/https://www.pastemagazine.com/tv/netflix/black-mirror-season-6-review|url-status=live}}</ref> Dissenting critics included ''[[The A.V. Club]]''{{'}}s Kayleigh Dray, who believed it was one of the strongest, and ''Den of Geek''{{'}}s Alec Bojalad, who found it middling.<ref name="DoG review">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-review-mazey-day/|title=Black Mirror Season 6 Episode 4 Review: Mazey Day|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Bojalad|first=Alec|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=28 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628123656/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-review-mazey-day/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="AVClub">{{cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/black-mirror-season-6-tv-review-netflix-charlie-brooker-1850540964|title=''Black Mirror'' season 6 review: Through the past, darkly|website=[[The A.V. Club]]|last=Dray|first=Kayleigh|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=20 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720184040/https://www.avclub.com/black-mirror-season-6-tv-review-netflix-charlie-brooker-1850540964|url-status=live}}</ref>

The episode's focus on paparazzi culture was poorly received. ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]''{{'}}s Richard Lawson said it would have been more relevant 15 years ago, with Armstrong and ''The Independent''{{'}}s Nick Hilton concurring that the subject matter was heavy-handed and dated.<ref name="Indy">{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-episodes-ranked-b2357292.html|title=Black Mirror season six review: Charlie Brooker's sci-fi mishmash needs to stop messing with a winning formula|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|last=Hilton|first=Nick|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616020939/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-episodes-ranked-b2357292.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BBC"/><ref name="Vanity review">{{cite web|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review|title=''Black Mirror''{{'}}s Odd Future Feels Stuck in the Past|work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|last=Lawson|first=Richard|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=20 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620063648/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review|url-status=live}}</ref> Chilton wrote that the same themes were more creatively explored in the film ''[[Nightcrawler (film)|Nightcrawler]]'' (2014).<ref name="Indy twist"/> ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]''{{'}}s Rachel Dodes described the moral as "trite" and ''i''{{'}}s Emily Baker said it was "already widely accepted" that a "ferocious appetite" for celebrity unhappiness was wrong.<ref name="i">{{cite web|url=https://inews.co.uk/culture/television/black-mirror-mazey-day-netflix-review-paparazzi-parable-2414515|title=Black Mirror: Mazey Day, Netflix, review: Celebrity privacy parable is all bark and no bite|work=[[i (newspaper)|i]]|last=Baker|first=Emily|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=15 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230615211337/https://inews.co.uk/culture/television/black-mirror-mazey-day-netflix-review-paparazzi-parable-2414515|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Esquire">{{cite web|url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a44215185/black-mirror-season-6-review/|title=''Black Mirror'' Season 6: Every Episode, Reviewed|work=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]|last=Dodes|first=Rachel|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=14 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230714071141/https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a44215185/black-mirror-season-6-review/|url-status=live}}</ref> Webster opined that the episode's premise is not explored with nuance due to the episode's brevity.<ref name="Verge"/> Of all the sixth series episodes, Sepinwall found it "most in need of extra time".<ref name="RS"/> In contrast, Bojalad believed it succeeds as a "cautionary tale about human nature" and saw its short runtime as a positive.<ref name="DoG review"/>

Mazey's transformation into a werewolf was also met with backlash.<ref name="ScreenRant"/> Rosenstock opined that it was both narratively and thematically lacking,<ref name="Vulture"/> while Sepinwall found it unintentionally funny.<ref name="RS"/> Harrisson criticised that supernatural elements break the "promise" established by the genre and history of the show. She said the viewer would experience "far less of a nonsensical shock" if "Demon 79" were viewed first.<ref name="DoG order"/> ''[[The New York Observer]]''{{'}}s Laura Babiak did not experience suspense or a feeling of horror during her viewing.<ref name="Observer">{{cite web|url=https://observer.com/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review-ranking-the-new-episodes-from-best-to-worst/|title='Black Mirror' Season 6 Review: Ranking the New Episodes from Best to Worst|work=[[The New York Observer]]|last=Babiak|first=Laura|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=20 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620151707/https://observer.com/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review-ranking-the-new-episodes-from-best-to-worst/|url-status=live}}</ref> In ''[[IGN]]'', Samantha Nelson contrasted it with ''[[From Dusk till Dawn]]'' (1996), saying the latter had a successful tonal shift but "Mazey Day" undermines its twist "by trying to make its final moments emotionally stirring".<ref name="IGN">{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/black-mirror-season-6-review|title=Black Mirror Season 6 Review|work=[[IGN]]|last=Nelson|first=Samantha|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=16 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230716085553/https://www.ign.com/articles/black-mirror-season-6-review|url-status=live}}</ref>

Some critics, however, praised the twist. Bojalad reviewed that there was "exactly the correct amount" of foreshadowing, including Mazey's driver's [[rivet gun]] and the rehab setup. Mazey's turmoil over becoming a werewolf, according to Bojalad, "plays better on a repeated viewing".<ref name="DoG review"/> Dodes praised that the ending was "so surprising and clever" as to justify deviation from ''Black Mirror''{{'}}s norms.<ref name="Esquire"/> Ed Power praised the twist as an "old-school thrill ride" in ''The Daily Telegraph''.<ref name="Tele">{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2023/06/15/black-mirror-series-6-episode-4-mazey-day-netflix-review/|title=Black Mirror, Mazey Day, review: a thrilling snapshot of early Noughties celeb culture|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Power|first=Ed|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=3 August 2023|archive-date=28 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628145412/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2023/06/15/black-mirror-series-6-episode-4-mazey-day-netflix-review/|url-status=live}}</ref> With ambivalent reactions, Baker said the twist was not bad but lacked inventiveness or novelty, while Webster found the last shot "fitting" but "a little on the nose".<ref name="Verge"/>

The characters received mixed reception. Bojalad and Power praised Beetz's acting, the latter describing her as "wonderfully bare-knuckle".<ref name="DoG review"/><ref name="Tele"/> Power reviewed that Mazey is "sympathetically portrayed by Rugaard as a little lost party girl".<ref name="Tele"/> However, paparazzi other than Bo were criticised: Webster found it "impossible to root for" them.<ref name="Verge"/> Bojalad found them "properly slimy but also quite tiring".<ref name="DoG review"/> Rosenstock questioned the narrative purpose of Nathan.<ref name="Vulture"/>

=== Episode rankings ===
"Mazey Day" was ranked by critics as one of the worst of the 28 instalments of ''Black Mirror'':
{{col-begin}}
{{col-2}}
* 14th – Ed Power, ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/on-demand/0/black-mirror-best-episodes-worst-ranked/|title=Black Mirror: every episode, ranked from best to worst|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Power|first=Ed|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=25 July 2023|archive-date=15 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115155347/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/on-demand/0/black-mirror-best-episodes-worst-ranked/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 16th – Amit Katwala, Matt Reynolds and James Temperton, ''[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]''<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/story/best-black-mirror-episodes/|title=Every ''Black Mirror'' Episode, From Worst to Best|magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]|last1=Katwala|first1=Amit|last2=Reynolds|first2=Matt|last3=Temperton|first3=James|date=21 June 2023|accessdate=25 July 2023|archive-date=24 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724172410/https://www.wired.com/story/best-black-mirror-episodes/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 23rd – James Hibbs, ''[[Radio Times]]''<ref name="RT ranking">{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/best-black-mirror-episodes/|title=Black Mirror: All 28 episodes ranked from worst to best|work=[[Radio Times]]|last=Hibbs|first=James|date=23 June 2023|accessdate=25 July 2023|archive-date=29 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230629000202/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/best-black-mirror-episodes/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 24th – Lucy Ford, Jack King and Brit Dawson, ''[[GQ]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/article/all-28-black-mirror-episodes-ranked|title=All 28 ''Black Mirror'' episodes (including season 6), ranked|work=[[GQ]]|last1=Ford|first1=Lucy|last2=King|first2=Jack|last3=Dawson|first3=Brit|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=25 July 2023|archive-date=24 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724134847/https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/article/all-28-black-mirror-episodes-ranked|url-status=live}}</ref>
{{col-2}}
* 26th – [[James Hibberd (writer)|James Hibberd]] and Christian Holub, ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]''<ref name="EW ranking">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-episodes-ranked/?slide=9f3e790b-33bf-4cd0-8bd1-d18a275e3286#9f3e790b-33bf-4cd0-8bd1-d18a275e3286|title=Every ''Black Mirror'' episode ranked|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|last1=Hibberd|first1=James|author-link=James Hibberd (writer)|last2=Holub|first2=Christian|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=25 July 2023|archive-date=25 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725133620/https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-episodes-ranked/?slide=14afdc5d-f174-453a-9089-72a1df4ca3a0#14afdc5d-f174-453a-9089-72a1df4ca3a0|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 26th – Charles Bramesco, ''[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]''<ref name="Vulture ranking">{{cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/2016/10/every-black-mirror-episode-from-worst-to-best.html|title=Every ''Black Mirror'' Episode, Ranked|work=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]|last=Bramesco|first=Charles|date=17 June 2023|accessdate=25 July 2023|archive-date=22 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210222050729/https://www.vulture.com/2016/10/every-black-mirror-episode-from-worst-to-best.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 28th – Brady Langmann, ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]''<ref name="Esquire ranking">{{cite web|url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a49919/black-mirror-episodes-ranked/|title=All 28 Episodes of ''Black Mirror'', Ranked|last1=Atad|first1=Corey|last2=Miller|first2=Matt|last3=Langmann|first3=Brady|work=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]|date=7 July 2023|accessdate=25 July 2023|archive-date=26 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161026080710/https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a49919/black-mirror-episodes-ranked/|url-status=live}}</ref>
{{col-end}}

''GamesRadar+'' and ''[[IndieWire]]'' listed the 27 episodes, excluding ''[[Black Mirror: Bandersnatch|Bandersnatch]]'', where "Mazey Day" placed 18th and 26th, respectively.<ref name="GamesRadar ranking">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/best-black-mirror-episodes/|title=All Black Mirror episodes ranked, from Be Right Back to Beyond the Sea|work=[[GamesRadar+]]|last=West|first=Amy|date=23 June 2023|accessdate=25 July 2023|archive-date=30 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230630173026/https://www.gamesradar.com/best-black-mirror-episodes/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/best-of/best-black-mirror-episodes-worst-netflix-ranked-1201897973/|title=Every 'Black Mirror' Episode, Ranked|work=[[IndieWire]]|last1=Greene|first1=Steve|last2=Khosla|first2=Proma|date=20 June 2023|accessdate=25 July 2023|archive-date=2 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230702125946/https://www.indiewire.com/features/best-of/best-black-mirror-episodes-worst-netflix-ranked-1201897973/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''The New York Observer'' described it as the worst of the five episodes in series six.<ref name="Observer"/> Writing for [[MSN]] Thomas West rated the episode as the worst of the entire series.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MSN |url=https://www.msn.com/en-gb/entertainment/tv/the-worst-episodes-from-20-iconic-tv-shows/ss-AA1HJpVW?ocid=msedgdhp&pc=U531&cvid=69fbb166c7184c46a1880794d8d41635&ei=11 |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=www.msn.com}}</ref>
